findings.claim: 1. [row A15] `until_bash: '[ "$bench.output.decision" = "approve" ] || ...'` reads a wait whose own `when: "$docket.output.ask == true"` (:434) skips it on most rounds. loop-nodes.md:695-697 says: "A skipped wait has no output, so an until_bash that reads a wait its own when: can skip fails the group."
findings.failure_scenario: Round 1 gets ANOTHER PASS with attempts < 5, so docket gives case none and ask false. bench is skipped, until_bash reads a skipped wait, and the hearing group fails. That fails spec-review and gauntlet-run on an ordinary revise round. plan-review-design.md:281 has the same form.

findings.claim: 2. [row A15] The same until_bash wraps the substituted reference in double quotes. loop-nodes.md:667-670 says: "Archon already single-quotes a substituted value, so \"$review.output.decision\" compares 'approve' with the quotes included and never matches".
findings.failure_scenario: The owner picks approve on a READY round, or confirm on an INVALID round. The test compares `'approve'` (quotes included) with `approve`, which is false, so the loop never ends on approval. Each answer allows one more iteration (workflow-language.md:773), so the phase cannot close and the speccer files another round after every approval. plan-review-design.md:281 has the same form.

findings.claim: 3. [row H27] close returns its result "for the latest ruling whose decision is an OwnerCase \"ends\"". But a ruling is written only by node `record` (:341, `when: "$LOOP_PREV.bench.output.decision != ''"`) at the start of the NEXT iteration. When the owner approves or confirms, until_bash ends the loop, so no next iteration runs and the ending ruling is never written.
findings.failure_scenario: READY, then the owner approves, then the loop ends. No `<slug>.ruling.N.txt` holds decision approve. `close` finds no ending ruling: it either fails or returns no outcome. `enter` (:448) does not copy, and `handoff` reports outcome "" with spec "" for an approved spec. The core also replaces plan review's working close rule ("latest round N with a summary", plan-review-design.md:137), so plan review breaks the same way once it runs on rounds.py (:124).

findings.claim: 4. [row H29] The design says "mode \"state\" inside the loop also passes INPUTS_START" (:90), and slot = 1 + retire reviews with N > start (:98). But in-loop nodes `filing` (:351) and `ready` (:378) pass only `with: { mode: state, slug: <slug> }`, with no `start: $docket-in.output.start`.
findings.failure_scenario: Rerun on a slug whose earlier run had 12 LEADING reviews. If start is None and treated as 0, `ready` says next = vacant and `vacate` cancels the new run at once, against "A rerun starts again at arbitrate-1" (:23). Old rounds also fill run_rounds, so the cap case fires early. If None means 'latest tried round', each call resets start: slot stays a1 after a LEADING (a retired session keeps trying) and run_rounds stays 0.

findings.claim: 5. [rows H26, H29] Every ledger `with:` passes `slug: <slug>`, and `screen` builds `with: { file: gauntlet/specs/<slug>.$ready.output.round.txt }`. No node of the block outputs the slug: the state output (:95-97) has no slug and no file path, and :293 bars `$INPUTS` outside prompts and `bash:`. The node also builds a round-file name, which the Homes row at :476 assigns to rounds.py only.
findings.failure_scenario: The builder has no reference that gives the slug to the docket-in, filing, ready, record, flag, case, docket and close script nodes, or to screen's `file` input. The YAML as written cannot be built without a new state field or a node outside the design. plan-review-design.md:314 and :337 have the same gap.

findings.claim: 6. [internal] `allowed_tools: [Task, Bash]  # ... the role forbids the speccer's own Bash` gives the speccer itself Bash, and only its prompt keeps it from using it. The Homes rows forbid "the speccer or any other agent running Bash" (:482) and "any role reaching files by a built-in tool other than the spiker's Bash" (:483).
findings.failure_scenario: The speccer runs `cat src/...` or writes under `tests/` through its own Bash. That bypasses the `speccer.mcp.json` fence. Per finding 1.03, the `file` sandbox does not limit writes to `gauntlet/scratch/`. Source text can then reach a spec block, or tests/ can change, with nothing enforcing the Homes row.

findings.claim: 7. [row P2; CLAUDE.md 1.3/1.4] A fresh run on a task whose spec was already approved hears the whole spec again, then fails at `enter`. The design says a fresh run on the same task reads the same state (:59). But the speccer's opening rule ("Spec files already there: needed is true", :215) and the ledger (round = latest tried + 1) have no branch for an existing `approved/<slug>.txt`. `enter`'s `cp -n` then exits non-zero when that target exists.
findings.failure_scenario: An earlier run approved the spec, then stopped in a later phase, and the owner starts gauntlet-run again on the same task. The speccer and arbiter spend Opus rounds on a new block. The owner approves again. `enter` fails on "target present", `handoff` is skipped (none_failed_min_one_success), and the run stops over a file that already holds the approved spec.

findings.claim: 8. [row F4] The design says "No agent can reach gauntlet/specs/approved/ or gauntlet/scratch/ through the fence", and :53 says "No other agent reads it". But `speccer.mcp.json` sets `FENCE_READ` to `.` (:273), and the spiker holds the same server's read tools (:370).
findings.failure_scenario: The speccer or a spiker calls mcp__fence-files__read_file on gauntlet/scratch/<slug>/... or gauntlet/specs/approved/<slug>.txt and the fence allows it. A builder or fence test that pins the stated rule finds it false.

findings.claim: 9. [internal] The `report` prompt passes `verdict $case.output.case`, whose values are "review" or "invalid" (:161-162). The reporter role (:251) takes "its verdict, READY or INVALID" and branches on READY.
findings.failure_scenario: On a READY round the reporter gets "review", a value its role does not name. It has to guess the READY branch, or read the review file to recover the verdict.

findings.claim: 10. [row H27] The design states for plan review that "`enter` and `handoff` read `$close.output.file`. The plan review design is otherwise unchanged." But plan review's `handoff` (plan-review-design.md:400-405) depends on [open, enter], reads no close output, and builds the plan path itself.
findings.failure_scenario: The builder of spec-review step 7 cannot make plan review's handoff read `$close.output.file` without changing its depends_on and script body. The spec review design does not specify that change, while it claims nothing else changes.
